podcast.body: Featured on the 1967 album *Pisces Aquarius Capricorn and John Limited*, "Star Collector" is historically significant as the first known rock song to incorporate a synthesizer. The instrument's sound in the track is characterized as "razor sharp," with its notes produced by square sine waves, contributing to a brief synthesizer craze. "The song called Star Collector and when the synth comes in, notice how razor sharp it sounds. Those notes are represented by square sine waves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song featured the synthesizer's debut in the world of rock and roll, appearing as a quick, twenty-second solo. Despite this early appearance, few musicians initially took pure electronic music seriously, often viewing it as suitable only for odd effects. "It was a quick, twenty-second solo in a song by the monkeys called Star Collector."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is noted as one of the very first instances, if not the first, of a synthesizer being used on a record. "The monkeys were among the first, if not the very first, to use a synth on a record. This appeared in a 1967 song called Star Collector."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
